title: [Bug] GlobTool returns raw symlink paths in results but uses resolved real paths internally — causes downstream read_file/edit failures on macOS and symlinked workspaces

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue is a clear and actionable bug report regarding path inconsistency in GlobTool output when operating in symlinked workspaces or macOS /tmp directories. It provides detailed reproduction steps, root cause analysis, and explicit line numbers in the codebase.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: The fix is localized to resolving paths in a single source file (packages/core/src/tools/glob.ts) and adding/updating unit tests in packages/core/src/tools/glob.test.ts.

summary.problem: GlobTool returns raw symlink paths in result strings, leading to path mismatch errors in downstream tools (like read_file and edit) when executing in symlinked workspace directories or macOS /tmp environments.
summary.root_cause: In GlobTool.execute(), sortedAbsolutePaths maps sortedEntries using entry.fullpath(), which returns raw string path resolution from the glob library rather than canonical real paths.
summary.context: The glob library's entry.fullpath() does not perform realpath resolution on symlinks. Because file access validation and subsequent tools in gemini-cli resolve inputs via resolveToRealPath, returning unresolved symlink paths causes path comparison and file access errors.

steps: Update GlobTool.execute() to resolve entry.fullpath() to canonical real paths using resolveToRealPath when building sortedAbsolutePaths.
Ensure fallback handling is maintained if resolveToRealPath fails or if entry path cannot be resolved.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: GlobTool returns canonical symlink-resolved absolute paths in output results when executed within symlinked target directories.
verification_steps: Add unit tests in packages/core/src/tools/glob.test.ts that execute GlobTool against a symlinked directory.
Verify that returned paths in llmContent match canonical real paths rather than unresolved symlink paths.
